original_question: For the outer billiard about a planar oval gamma, consider the area spectrum consisting of the areas of polygons formed by periodic outer-billiard trajectories. Is this area spectrum related to the spectrum of some differential operator, analogously to how the length spectrum of an inner billiard is related to the Laplace spectrum by the Poisson summation formula?
target_in_paper: Serge Tabachnikov, Problem 5 (page 421): the open problem asking whether the area spectrum of the outer billiard about an oval γ is related to the spectrum of some differential operator.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct problem essentially verbatim: it is about the outer billiard about a planar oval γ, its area spectrum coming from periodic outer-billiard polygons, and the analogy with the usual billiard length spectrum and the Laplace spectrum via the Poisson summation formula.
missing_details: In the paper, an oval means a smooth closed strictly convex planar curve.
For full stand-alone clarity, the outer billiard map is the map T defined by the reflection law that for a point A outside γ, the segment [A,T(A)] is tangent to γ at its midpoint.
The paper specifies that the relevant polygons are the circumscribed polygons of extremal area arising from periodic outer-billiard trajectories.
On the comparison side, the paper refers specifically to the Dirichlet Laplace operator for the ordinary billiard in the domain bounded by γ.
The area spectrum is treated as a set of areas; the paper does not introduce multiplicities or any finer spectral counting data.
The paper asks only whether there is some relation to the spectrum of some differential operator; it does not specify the operator or the exact form of the relation.
The nearby remark about spherical duality between inner and outer billiards is contextual background, not part of the formal problem statement.
refined_question: Let γ be a planar oval, i.e. a smooth closed strictly convex curve, and let T be the outer billiard map about γ, defined so that for each point A outside γ the segment [A,T(A)] is tangent to γ at its midpoint. Consider the area spectrum of this outer billiard, namely the set of areas of the polygons formed by periodic T-trajectories, equivalently the circumscribed polygons of extremal area. Is this area spectrum related to the spectrum of some differential operator, analogously to the fact that the length spectrum of the ordinary billiard in the domain bounded by γ is related, via the Poisson summation formula, to the spectrum of the Dirichlet Laplacian on that domain?
justification: The nearest official formulation is Serge Tabachnikov's Problem 5 on page 421, and your draft matches it almost word for word. I kept the scope exactly there, adding only nearby definitions needed to make it stand-alone: the paper's local meaning of 'oval' as a smooth closed strictly convex planar curve (Serge Tabachnikov, Problem 2, page 419) and the standard outer-billiard reflection law stated earlier in the paper (Misha Bialy, Problem 2, page 412). I also retained the paper's parenthetical clarification that the periodic polygons are circumscribed polygons of extremal area, while avoiding any stronger reformulation involving a specified operator, multiplicities, or a trace formula, because the paper itself leaves all of that open.
